solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Nothing in handbag: contents oddly missing

indicators.note: the letters of the words in handbag are read with every odd-placed one dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Someone finds their handbag empty, as though its contents went astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word, but it belongs to the fodder: I-N-H-A-N-D-B-A-G with the odd letters gone leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish-derived slang for zero, used in English to mean not a thing.

clue.text: Most revolting wine kept in secluded place

indicators.note: one thing kept in another sits inside it, so the wine goes within the hideaway

parts.note: a nest is a snug, hidden retreat
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A disgusting bottle of wine has been stashed away in a hideout.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative synonym: the vilest or most disgusting thing is the one that revolts most.

clue.text: Government follower supporting party

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: a do is an informal party
a minion is a servile follower

explanation.surface: A political follower backs his party.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion means rule or sovereign authority over a territory, i.e. government.

clue.text: Lacking formal education, so he almost couldn't work

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: almost the whole word couldn't, its final letter cut off

explanation.surface: A man explains he could barely work because he never went to school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the T from COULDN'T; 'work' then rearranges SO HE COULDN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone never schooled has had no formal teaching, the literal sense of the word.

clue.text: Material collected by Lenin once

indicators.note: the letters are gathered up by the words that follow, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Some fabric that the Soviet leader Lenin once gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a lightweight sheer fabric of silk or nylon, a type of dress material.

clue.text: Drink for each individual child-minder?

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
per means for each, as in per person
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Tea is ordered for everyone, a separate cup each, at a babysitting job.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone supervises a young person, loosely a minder of a child, hence the question mark.

clue.text: During trip, public transport's unlikely to run well?

indicators.note: one thing happening during another lies within it, so the transport goes inside the trip

parts.note: an outing is a trip or excursion
the possessive read as 'of train'

explanation.surface: On an excursion, the trains are, as ever, not expected to run on time.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about trains running late; the definition is about an athlete who has stopped practising.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete who is unfit from lack of practice will not run well.

clue.text: Drink is sweet without ice

indicators.note: without means the frozen water is taken away from the sweet

parts.note: liquorice is a black chewy sweet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink is sugary and served with no ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is alcoholic drink, especially spirits.

clue.text: German fellow who'll eat less?

definitions.meaning: a common German masculine first name
someone on a slimming regime who cuts down on food

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one spelling: a German man's name and a person following a weight-loss diet.

clue.text: Animated character won't stop drinking when entertaining male

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so the drinking phrase surrounds the man

parts.note: someone who sips on keeps drinking

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure keeps drinking while hosting a man.
explanation.walkthrough: SIPS ON is split as SI-PS ON with M placed after SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer, Bart and family are the cartoon Simpsons, animated characters of the long-running TV show.

clue.text: The crises resolved by politician? Unlikely version of events

indicators.note: a thing resolved is broken down and worked out afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician claims to have sorted out the crises, which sounds improbable.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret history is an alternative, hidden account of events, often far-fetched or unofficial.

clue.text: Ancient opponent completely lacking that special quality

parts.note: someone anti is against a thing

indicators.note: lacking means the indefinable quality is removed from what precedes it

parts.note: quite means entirely or completely
'it' is a slang term for charisma or sex appeal

explanation.surface: An old rival has utterly lost his star quality.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTIQUITE loses the I and T from QUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique describes something very old, from a bygone era.

clue.text: Absence of sin, note, in local old churches

parts.note: a local is a British term for one's neighbourhood pub, an inn

indicators.note: in means the note sits inside the following string

parts.note: CE, Church of England, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A sinless state found at the local pub and the old churches.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is the neighbourhood pub in Britain. Two CE abbreviations stand for the churches, and N goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence is freedom from guilt or wrongdoing, i.e. being without sin.

clue.text: Didn't move back, having reached Zimbabwe's borders

parts.note: fro means back, as in to and fro

indicators.note: the borders of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A traveller stood still on returning once they had reached Zimbabwe's frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze is to stop dead and stay motionless.

clue.text: Report about one man's unusual craft

indicators.note: the report goes about, i.e. around, the jumbled letters

parts.note: a story is a news report

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A news item about one man's strange trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like a boat but means a trade; the 'unusual' anagram splits the report after its O.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonemasonry is the skilled trade of cutting and building with stone, a craft.

clue.text: A stroppier one hoisted banner

indicators.note: in a down clue hoisted means lifted higher, so the single letter is moved upwards

parts.note: bolshie is British slang for difficult or stroppy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A more truculent person raised a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banner' is not a flag but one who bans. In A BOLSHIER the I moves up two places.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner here is one who bans; one who abolishes things does just that.

clue.text: Assume I'm initially unknown, among list of candidates

indicators.note: among means set within the list

parts.note: a slate is a list of nominees for election
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone supposes they are an unknown on the ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: To simulate or assume a manner is to feign or put it on.

clue.text: At home, looked after fiancée

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
tended means cared for

explanation.surface: A man's betrothed is cared for at home.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one plans to marry, a betrothed bride-to-be.

clue.text: The artist said to employ natural substance, I think

indicators.note: to employ is to take on and hold, so the substance is held within

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: said means the painter's name is spoken, giving letters by sound

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter
ore is a naturally occurring mineral

explanation.surface: A painter is quoted as using a natural material.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the speaker's own words: someone who says 'I think' deals in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorist is one whose work is thinking, so 'I think' is the cryptic self-description.

clue.text: You want blemish-free crockery collection? That's a problem

indicators.note: free of something means without it, so the flaw is removed

parts.note: a tea service is a set of cups, saucers and pots
a vice is a fault or failing

explanation.surface: Someone wants a spotless tea set, which proves tricky.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzle or tricky question, a brain-teaser.

clue.text: Battles about retaining power over large urban development

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above what follows
retaining means keeping something inside
about means turned around, so the word for battles is read backwards

parts.note: wars are battles

explanation.surface: Conflicts over power spread across a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban sprawl is unplanned spreading growth of a city into the countryside.

clue.text: Officers no longer appearing in displays

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
POs are petty officers in the navy

explanation.surface: Retired officers turning up at exhibitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Expos are exhibitions or trade shows, places of public display.

clue.text: Start school?

definitions.meaning: to set up or found something
an educational establishment, especially one for technical or higher learning

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to found or begin, and the noun is an educational college or organisation.

clue.text: Numbers going up and down

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same upwards as downwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Figures that rise and fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers are pieces of music, and solos are pieces performed by one player.

clue.text: Scotsman's expression of disbelief, following marine creature here?

definitions.text: Scotsman's expression of disbelief, following marine creature here?

indicators.note: following places the Scottish exclamation after the animal

parts.note: a seal is a sea mammal
och is a Scottish exclamation of surprise or disbelief

explanation.surface: A Scot exclaims in surprise at seeing a seal in this place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea loch is a Scottish arm of the sea, just the place a seal would be spotted.

clue.text: Moving slowly, coach takes girl back

indicators.note: back means the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: a drag is an old horse-drawn private coach
gal is informal for girl

explanation.surface: A slow coach picks up a girl on its way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' joins the coach and girl; 'back' reverses DRAGGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Laggard describes someone falling behind, dawdling and slow.

clue.text: Car event run by friend leading to misfortune

indicators.note: leading to puts the earlier pieces before the misfortune

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an ally is a friend
a cross to bear is a misfortune or burden

explanation.surface: A motoring event organised by a pal ends in disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallycross is a motor sport combining racing on tarmac and dirt circuits.

clue.text: Make improvements to motorway border

parts.note: M is a British motorway, as in the M1
an end is a boundary or limit

explanation.surface: Roadworks to improve the edge of a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend is to repair, making something better.
